subject: Capstone P1 checks 25 and 28 are container-side (SANDBOX_CHALLENGES cmd:) and forgeable in isolation -- 28 in particular is a grep against apply-twice.txt, a file the student writes, so 'echo RUN 1; echo RUN 2; echo no changes' passes it. 26 and 27 are CLOUD_CHECKS fn: and genuinely unforgeable (26 reads the live cloud, 27 compares live ids against a SERVER-SIDE pre-teardown baseline), and they carry the lab's thesis, so forging 25/28 alone gains a student nothing structural. Decide: accept the mixed tier as designed and LABEL it honestly on the page, or move 28's idempotency evidence server-side (the applier could be re-run by the grader rather than trusting a transcript the student pastes). Measured on bc1 2026-08-01 by reading lab-manager/server.js.
description:
From Nancy PAUSE on the capstone hub link
[2026-08-01 00:36] GATE FAILED 2026-08-01. Ran bash qc-lab.sh project on bc1 (log: /home/eq1/qc-project-2026-08-01.log). Adversarial stage: cheats B and C correctly rejected by 25 and 26, but cheat E PASSED check 27 -- 'no baseline was ever recorded, so nothing was proven'. Root cause verified by reading /app/data/capstone-baselines.json inside the lab-manager container: baselines are keyed by UID ONLY and persist indefinitely across sessions. See BUG-077 [P1]. This ALSO downgrades my earlier claim that 27 is unforgeable -- it is unforgeable only for a student with no prior baseline.
[2026-08-01 01:09] GATE PASSED on the clean re-run (log: bc1 /home/eq1/qc-project-clean-2026-08-01.log). All four checks discriminate -- each seen both passing and failing. The earlier FAIL was harness debris, not a product defect; BUG-077 corrected P1 -> P3. The mixed-tier reasoning in this task therefore stands: 26 and 27 are server-side and both discriminate, so forging 25/28 alone still gains nothing structural. Residual: cross-attempt stale baseline (BUG-077 P3).

notes.text:
BUG-077 OPTION D IS VIABLE -- MEASURED, not assumed. This was the option Nancy said must not win by default 'because A has a known cost and D's cost is merely undiscovered'. It is now discovered and it is good.
Nova's changes-since filter RETURNS DELETED INSTANCES. Queried from a lab container with a PROJECT-SCOPED application credential (no admin):
    GET <compute>/servers                                  -> 0 live
    GET <compute>/servers/detail?changes-since=2020-01-01   -> 8 records, ALL status=DELETED
    each carries OS-SRV-USG:terminated_at, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:59:02, 2026-07-31T18:46:55
THE FIX THIS ENABLES: check 27 records the baseline's server ids AND its timestamp, then at grade time requires every baseline server id to appear with status=DELETED and terminated_at AFTER baseline.at. That verifies the teardown POSITIVELY -- 'you destroyed these, after you recorded them' -- instead of inferring it from absence, which is the entire bug (absence cannot tell 'destroyed just now' from 'gone weeks ago').
NO STRAND RISK, which is why this beats option A (session-scoping). The deletion record lives in Nova, not in a session, so a student who records a baseline, tears down, loses their container and returns tomorrow still passes. That strand was the reason A was unacceptable.
TWO HONEST LIMITS, neither measured yet:
  RETENTION. The oldest record here is ~1 day old (2026-07-31T09:38). Nova archives deleted rows eventually (reclaim_instance_interval / DB archiving). If a student's baseline is older than retention, the record is gone and the check would fail an honest student. Retention on this deployment is UNKNOWN and must be measured before this ships.
  SERVERS ONLY. This is a Nova capability. Check 27's baseline also covers NETWORKS, and Neutron has no changes-since equivalent. So servers can be verified positively; networks would still be inferred from absence. Partial, but servers are the stronger signal and the one the thesis rests on.

BUG-077 OPTION D -- RETENTION GAP CLOSED 2026-08-01. This was the one honest unknown left after establishing that Nova changes-since returns deleted instances with terminated_at timestamps.
Checked on bc2: NO reclaim_instance_interval configured in /etc/nova/nova.conf, and NO archive or purge cron in either the user or root crontab. Nothing runs `nova-manage db archive_deleted_rows`. So deleted-instance rows are never purged from the Nova DB, and changes-since keeps returning them indefinitely.
The ~1 day I observed empirically (oldest record 2026-07-31T09:38) is the AGE OF THE POOL'S ACTIVITY, not a retention ceiling. Stated that way deliberately -- I cannot prove unlimited retention from an absence of old data, only from the absence of anything that deletes it. If an archive job is ever added, this check degrades SILENTLY: an honest student with a baseline older than the new window would start failing, and nothing would explain why. That belongs in a comment next to the check.
SO OPTION D IS FULLY VIABLE FOR SERVERS. Remaining limit unchanged: Neutron has no changes-since equivalent, so NETWORKS in the baseline would still be inferred from absence. Servers carry the thesis.
STATUS: BUG-077 fix is DESIGNED and measured. Building it is a bc1 lab-manager/server.js change -- production infrastructure -- so it needs the operator, not just a design pass.
